Project Summary

This project aims to identify suitable regions on Mars for future human exploration and settlement. We evaluated three candidate sites (AP-1, AP-8, and AP-9) and developed an additional alternative region, UC-06, through our own research and analysis. By examining terrain conditions, subsurface water ice potential, mineral resources, radiation levels, and environmental risks, we compared the advantages and limitations of each location.

Based on our findings, we developed an integrated model combining AP-8 as the primary landing and settlement site with UC-06 as a complementary research and resource center. We also designed a connecting route between the two locations and proposed an emergency shelter to improve mission safety.

Our project addresses the challenges of resource accessibility, landing safety, and operational continuity. It presents a multi-criteria approach to planning safer and more sustainable future human missions to Mars.
details:
About Our Project

Our project is about finding suitable locations on Mars for future human exploration and settlement. We wanted to understand which areas could offer better conditions for landing, living, and carrying out scientific research.

First, we studied three candidate regions: AP-1, AP-8, and AP-9. We also researched and identified a fourth location, UC-06, as our own alternative. While comparing these regions, we considered several factors, such as terrain, slope, possible underground water ice, mineral deposits, radiation levels, and environmental risks.

We used scientific information and maps related to NASA and ESA missions. These included MOLA topographic data, HRSC elevation models, and research on subsurface water ice, such as NASA's SWIM project. By examining and comparing these maps, we tried to understand the strengths and weaknesses of each location.

As a result, we chose AP-8 as our main landing and settlement area because of its relatively flat terrain and proximity to potential water ice resources. We selected UC-06 as a second location because it is close to mineral deposits and offers opportunities for geological research. We also planned a route between the two locations and included an emergency shelter in our design.

One of the most important parts of our project is that we did not limit ourselves to the three existing candidate sites. We came up with our own alternative, UC-06, and combined it with AP-8 in a plan where the two locations support each other. We also considered transportation and safety instead of focusing only on choosing a landing site.

We hope our project can contribute to future Mars missions by showing how different locations and resources can be evaluated together to create a safer and more practical exploration plan.
